p.src: Now the Handsome Monkey King returned home in triumph after vanquishing the Demon King of Havoc and seizing a great sword. Every day he practiced martial arts, having the young monkeys cut bamboo into standards, carve wood into swords, make banners, and sound whistles as they advanced and retreated, pitched camp and set up stockades, amusing themselves thus for a long while. One day, while sitting quietly, he reflected: “Our games here may someday become earnest. We might alarm a human king, or some king of birds or beasts might take offense and accuse us of drilling troops for rebellion, then raise an army to attack us. You have only bamboo poles and wooden swords—how could you face an enemy? We must have sharp swords and halberds. What are we to do?” Hearing this, the monkeys were all alarmed and said, “Your Majesty sees far ahead, but there is nowhere we can obtain such weapons.” As they spoke, four old monkeys came forward—two bare-bottomed macaques and two long-armed apes. Approaching him, they said, “Your Majesty, if you wish to procure sharp weapons, it is easily done.” Wukong asked, “How is it easy?” The four monkeys replied, “Two hundred li across the waters east of our mountain lies the territory of the Kingdom of Aolai. That land has a king upon its throne and countless soldiers and civilians throughout its cities, so it must surely have craftsmen who work gold, silver, bronze, and iron. If Your Majesty goes there, you could buy or commission some weapons and train us with them to defend our mountain. That would indeed be the means to preserve our peace and prosperity for many years.” Wukong was delighted to hear this and said, “Stay here and amuse yourselves until I return.”

p.src: When the wind arose, it terrified and scattered the ruler and people of Aolai. Throughout every market and street, all hurriedly shut their doors, and no one dared venture outside. Only then did Wukong lower his cloud. He charged straight through the palace gates and searched until he found the armory and military storehouse. Opening the doors, he saw countless weapons within: sabers, spears, swords, halberds, axes, battle-axes, sickle-spears, scythes, whips, rakes, maces, iron clubs, rods, bows, crossbows, forks, and lances—every kind was there. Delighted at the sight, he said, “How many can I carry by myself? I had better use the art of multiplying myself to move them all.” The splendid Monkey King plucked out a handful of hairs, chewed them to pieces in his mouth, spat them forth, recited an incantation, and cried, “Transform!” They changed into hundreds upon hundreds of little monkeys, who snatched up and carried off the weapons in a frenzy. The strong took five or seven apiece, while the weaker took two or three, until they had emptied the place completely. Wukong stepped directly onto his cloud, worked a transporting spell, summoned the gale back, and led the little monkeys home.

p.src: Meanwhile, the monkeys great and small of the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit were playing outside the cave entrance. Suddenly they heard the roar of the wind and saw the sky crowded from end to end with a boundless host of monkey spirits. Terrified, they scattered and hid. Presently the Handsome Monkey King lowered his cloud and dispersed the mist. With a shake of his body, he recalled the hairs, then piled all the weapons in disorder before the mountain and cried, “Little ones, come and claim your weapons!” When the monkeys looked, they saw Wukong standing alone on the level ground. They all ran over, kowtowed, and asked what had happened. Wukong recounted the whole affair—how he had raised the gale and carried off the weapons. After thanking him, the monkeys rushed to seize sabers and swords, snatched axes and fought over spears, drew bows and cocked crossbows, and spent the whole day shouting and drilling.

p.src: The next day, they drew up their camp as before. Wukong assembled the entire monkey host and counted more than forty-seven thousand among them. By now they had alarmed all the strange beasts throughout the mountain—wolves, great serpents, tigers, leopards, river deer, muntjacs, roebucks, wild dogs, foxes, civets, badgers, raccoon dogs, lions, elephants, suanni, orangutans, bears, deer, wild boars, mountain oxen, antelopes, blue rhinoceroses, jiao beasts, divine mastiffs, and many others. The demon kings of all seventy-two caves came to pay homage and acknowledge the Monkey King as their sovereign. Every year they brought tribute, and at all four seasons they answered the roll call. Some joined the ranks for drill, while others gathered provisions as each season required. Everything was kept in perfect order, making the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit as impregnable as an iron barrel and a fortress of gold. The demon kings of the various regions also presented gongs and drums, colored banners, helmets, and armor. Amid the endless bustle, every day they practiced maneuvers and prepared their forces.

p.src: While the Handsome Monkey King was rejoicing, he suddenly said to the assembly, “You are well practiced with bows and crossbows and skilled in the use of weapons, but this sword of mine is truly clumsy and unwieldy. It does not suit me at all. What am I to do?” The four old monkeys stepped forward and reported, “Your Majesty is an immortal sage; ordinary weapons are unworthy of your use. But may we ask whether Your Majesty can travel beneath the water?” Wukong replied, “Since learning the Way, I have mastered the seventy-two earthly transformations, and my somersault cloud possesses immeasurable divine power. I am adept at becoming invisible, concealing my form, casting spells, and transporting things by magic. There is a road for me into Heaven and a gate for me beneath the earth. I can walk through sunlight or moonlight without casting a shadow and pass through metal or stone without hindrance. Water cannot drown me, nor fire burn me. Where could I possibly be unable to go?” The four monkeys said, “Since Your Majesty possesses such divine powers, know that the waters beneath our Iron Slab Bridge lead to the Dragon Palace of the Eastern Sea. If Your Majesty would descend there, seek out the old Dragon King, and ask him for some weapon, would you not find one perfectly to your liking?” Wukong was greatly delighted to hear this and said, “Wait here until I return.”

p.src: The fine Monkey King leapt to the bridgehead, cast a water-parting spell, made the proper hand sign, and plunged with a splash into the waves. Parting a path through the water, he went straight to the bottom of the Eastern Ocean. As he went, a yaksha patrolling the sea suddenly appeared and barred his way, asking, “Who is the divine personage coming through the parted waters? State your identity clearly, so that I may report your arrival and have you welcomed.” Wukong said, “I am Sun Wukong, the Heaven-born Sage of the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. I am a close neighbor of your old Dragon King. How is it that you do not know me?” Hearing this, the yaksha hurried back to the Crystal Palace and reported, “Your Majesty, outside is Sun Wukong, the Heaven-born Sage of the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He calls himself Your Majesty’s close neighbor and is approaching the palace.” Ao Guang, Dragon King of the Eastern Ocean, rose at once and went out with his dragon sons and grandsons, shrimp soldiers, and crab generals to welcome him. “Exalted Immortal, please come in, please come in.” Once they had met inside the palace, Wukong was seated in the place of honor and served tea. The Dragon King then asked, “When did the Exalted Immortal attain the Way? And what immortal arts were you taught?” Wukong said, “After I came into the world, I left home to cultivate the Way and gained a body beyond birth and death. Recently, while drilling my children and grandchildren to defend our mountain cave, I found myself without a weapon. I have long heard that my worthy neighbor enjoys the splendors of a jasper palace and shell-built halls, and surely possesses divine weapons to spare. I have therefore come especially to ask you for one.” On hearing this, the Dragon King could hardly refuse. He ordered Commander Mandarin Fish to bring out a great pole-mounted saber and present it to Wukong. Wukong said, “Old Sun does not know how to wield a saber. Please grant me another weapon.” The Dragon King next ordered Colonel Whitefish to lead the eel strongmen in carrying out a nine-pronged fork. Wukong leapt down, took it in his hands, and went through a whole routine. Then he put it down and said, “Too light, too light, too light! It does not suit my hand. Please grant me another.” The Dragon King laughed. “Exalted Immortal, you have not noticed that this fork weighs three thousand six hundred catties.” Wukong said, “It does not suit my hand. It does not suit my hand.” The Dragon King grew afraid and ordered Admiral Bream and General Carp to carry out a painted-shafted square-bladed halberd. The halberd weighed seven thousand two hundred catties. When Wukong saw it, he hurried forward and took it in his hands. He struck several postures, displayed a couple of techniques, then planted it upright and said, “Still too light, too light, too light.” The old Dragon King became more frightened than ever. “Exalted Immortal, this halberd is the heaviest weapon in my palace. I have no other weapons left.” Wukong laughed. “As the ancients said, ‘Never fear that the Dragon King of the Sea has no treasure!’ Go and search once more. If you find anything to my liking, I shall pay its full value.” The Dragon King said, “There truly is nothing else.”

In our treasury of the sea is that divine iron which once fixed the bed of the River of Heaven. For the past few days it has glowed with brilliant rosy light and streamed with auspicious vapors. Could it be that the time has come for it to appear and meet this sage?” The Dragon King said, “When Great Yu controlled the floods, that object was used as a gauge to determine the depths of rivers and seas. It is merely a piece of divine iron. What use could it be?” The Dragon Queen said, “Never mind whether he can use it. Just give it to him and let him alter it however he pleases. All that matters is getting him out of the palace.” The old Dragon King followed her advice and told Wukong everything. Wukong said, “Bring it out and let me see it.” The Dragon King waved his hands. “It cannot be shouldered or carried. The Exalted Immortal must go and see it himself.” Wukong asked, “Where is it? Lead me there.”

p.src: The Dragon King duly led him into the heart of the sea treasury, where they suddenly beheld ten thousand shafts of golden light. Pointing, the Dragon King said, “The object giving off that light is the one.” Wukong lifted his robe and stepped forward to feel it. It proved to be an iron pillar, roughly the thickness of a peck measure and over twenty feet long. He grasped it with both hands and exerted all his strength. “It is much too thick and long. It would be usable if only it were shorter and thinner.” As soon as he finished speaking, the treasure shortened by several feet and became a measure slimmer. Wukong hefted it again and said, “It would be better still if it were a little thinner.” The treasure truly did become somewhat thinner again. Wukong was delighted. When he carried it out of the sea treasury and examined it, he found that it had a golden band at either end and a length of black iron between them. Close beside one band was an engraved line of characters: “As-You-Will Gold-Banded Cudgel, weight thirteen thousand five hundred catties.” Secretly delighted, he thought, “This treasure must obey its owner’s wishes.” As he walked, he thought and murmured, hefting it in his hand. “It would be finer still if it were shorter and thinner.” By the time he brought it outside, it was only about twenty feet long and as thick as the mouth of a bowl.

p.src: Just look at him display his magic powers, unleashing his techniques and whirling about the Crystal Palace. The old Dragon King was terrified out of his wits, and the young dragon princes nearly lost their souls. Turtles, soft-shelled turtles, giant turtles, and alligators drew in their necks, while fish, shrimp, great turtles, and crabs hid their heads. Holding the treasure in his hand, Wukong seated himself in the Crystal Palace and said to the Dragon King with a smile, “Many thanks for my worthy neighbor’s generosity.” The Dragon King said, “Think nothing of it, think nothing of it.” Wukong said, “This piece of iron is useful enough, but there is still another matter.” The Dragon King asked, “What else does the Exalted Immortal have to say?” Wukong said, “If this iron had not been here, that would have been the end of it; but now that I hold it in my hand, I have no clothing or armor to match it. What am I to do? If you have a suit of armor here, you may as well give it to me too, and I shall thank you for everything together.” The Dragon King said, “That, however, I do not have.” Wukong said, “A guest should not trouble two hosts. If you have none, then I certainly shall not leave through this gate.” The Dragon King said, “May I trouble the Exalted Immortal to visit another sea? Perhaps one may be found there.” Wukong replied, “Better to sit in one house than visit three. You must by all means find me a suit.” The Dragon King said, “I truly have none. If I did, I would certainly present it to you.” Wukong said, “You truly have none? Then let me test this iron on you!” The Dragon King panicked. “Exalted Immortal, do not strike, do not strike! Let me see whether my younger brothers have anything. We shall present you with a suit.” Wukong asked, “Where are your younger brothers?” The Dragon King said, “My younger brothers are Ao Qin, Dragon King of the Southern Ocean; Ao Shun, Dragon King of the Northern Ocean; and Ao Run, Dragon King of the Western Ocean.” Wukong said, “Old Sun will not go, will not go. As the saying goes, ‘Three promised on credit are not worth two in hand.’ I merely ask that you accommodate yourself to what is available and give me a suit.” The old Dragon King said, “There is no need for the Exalted Immortal to go. I have an iron drum and a golden bell here. Whenever an urgent matter arises, we beat the drum and strike the bell, and my younger brothers arrive in an instant.” Wukong said, “If that is so, hurry and beat the drum and strike the bell.” And indeed, the alligator general went off to strike the bell, while the soft-shelled-turtle marshal came to beat the drum.

p.src: Before long, the sounding bells and drums duly startled the Dragon Kings of the other three seas. In a moment they arrived and met together outside. Ao Qin said, “Elder Brother, what urgent matter made you beat the drums and strike the bells?” The old Dragon King said, “Dear brother, it is a sorry tale. A certain heaven-born sage from the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit came this morning and claimed me as his neighbor. Then he asked for a weapon. When I offered him a steel fork, he found it too small; when I presented a decorated halberd, he found it too light. He took out for himself the divine iron that anchors the bed of the River of Heaven and displayed a few of his tricks with it. Now he is sitting in the palace demanding some manner of armor as well. I have none here, so I sounded the bells and drums to summon you, my brothers. If any of you have armor to spare, give him a suit and send him on his way.” On hearing this, Ao Qin flew into a rage. “Why do we brothers not muster our troops and seize him?” The old Dragon King said, “Do not speak of seizing him! Do not speak of it! That iron of his kills at the lightest swing and slays at the slightest knock. The merest touch breaks the skin; the faintest graze tears the sinews.” Ao Run, Dragon King of the Western Sea, said, “Second Brother, you must not fight him. Let us simply put together a suit of armor for him and send him away. Then we can submit a memorial to Heaven, and Heaven itself will punish him.” Ao Shun, Dragon King of the Northern Sea, said, “That is well said. u.src: Before long, the sounding bells and drums duly startled the Dragon Kings of the other three seas. In a moment they arrived and met together outside.
Ao Qin said, “Elder Brother, what urgent matter made you beat the drums and strike the bells?”
The old Dragon King said, “Dear brother, it is a sorry tale.
A certain heaven-born sage from the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit came this morning and claimed me as his neighbor.
Then he asked for a weapon. When I offered him a steel fork, he found it too small; when I presented a decorated halberd, he found it too light.
He took out for himself the divine iron that anchors the bed of the River of Heaven and displayed a few of his tricks with it.
Now he is sitting in the palace demanding some manner of armor as well.
I have none here, so I sounded the bells and drums to summon you, my brothers.
If any of you have armor to spare, give him a suit and send him on his way.”
On hearing this, Ao Qin flew into a rage. “Why do we brothers not muster our troops and seize him?”
The old Dragon King said, “Do not speak of seizing him! Do not speak of it!
That iron of his kills at the lightest swing and slays at the slightest knock.
The merest touch breaks the skin; the faintest graze tears the sinews.”
Ao Run, Dragon King of the Western Sea, said, “Second Brother, you must not fight him.
Let us simply put together a suit of armor for him and send him away. Then we can submit a memorial to Heaven, and Heaven itself will punish him.”

p.src: Now behold the Monkey King: parting the waters, he went straight back to the Iron Slab Bridge and leaped up beside it. There he saw the four elder monkeys leading the whole troop, all waiting beside the bridge. Suddenly they saw Wukong spring from the waves without a drop of water upon him and stride onto the bridge in a blaze of gold. The monkeys were so astonished that they all knelt down and cried, “Your Majesty, how splendid you look! How splendid you look!” Wukong, his face radiant with delight, mounted his jeweled throne and stood the iron staff upright in the middle. Not knowing their own limits, the monkeys all came to lift the treasure, but they were like dragonflies trying to shake an iron tree and could not budge it in the slightest. Each bit his finger and stuck out his tongue, exclaiming, “Good heavens! It is so heavy—how ever did you manage to bring it here?” Wukong stepped forward, opened his hand, and snatched it up in one grasp. Laughing, he told the monkeys, “Every object has its rightful master. This treasure had lain in the treasury of the sea for no one knows how many thousands of years, and by a happy chance it gave off light this very year. The Dragon King took it for nothing but a lump of black iron, though it was also called the Divine Treasure that Anchored the Bed of the River of Heaven. Those fellows could not carry or lift it, so they asked me to go and take it myself. At the time, this treasure was over twenty feet long and as thick as a grain measure. When I seized it, I thought it too large, and it immediately grew much smaller. I bade it grow smaller again, and again it shrank greatly. I bade it grow smaller once more, and once more it shrank greatly. I quickly held it up to the daylight and saw a line of words upon it: ‘As-You-Will Gold-Banded Staff, weight thirteen thousand five hundred catties.’ All of you stand back and watch me make it change again.” He balanced the treasure in his hand and cried, “Smaller! Smaller! Smaller!” At once it shrank to the size of an embroidery needle, small enough to be tucked away inside his ear. The monkeys were dumbfounded and cried, “Your Majesty, take it out and play with it some more!” The Monkey King truly did take it from his ear. Holding it on his palm, he cried, “Larger! Larger! Larger!” At once it again became as thick as a grain measure and some twenty feet long. At the height of his delight, he sprang onto the bridge and strode out of the cave. Gripping the treasure in his hand, he exercised the divine power of imitating Heaven and Earth, bent at the waist, and cried, “Grow!” He grew to a height of ten thousand fathoms, with a head like Mount Tai, a waist like a steep range of peaks, eyes like lightning, a mouth like a basin of blood, and teeth like swords and halberds. The staff in his hand reached upward to the Thirty-third Heaven and downward to the eighteenth level of Hell. The tigers, leopards, wolves, and other beasts, all the mountain monsters, and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves were so terrified that they knocked their heads upon the ground in homage, trembling as their souls nearly fled their bodies. In an instant he withdrew his colossal form, changed the treasure back into an embroidery needle, hid it in his ear, and returned to his cave dwelling. In their alarm, the demon kings of all the caves came to pay homage and offer congratulations.

p.src: With his mind now at ease, each day he rode the clouds and mist, roaming the Four Seas and taking his pleasure among a thousand mountains. Displaying his martial arts, he sought out heroes everywhere. Exercising his magic powers, he befriended worthy companions far and wide. At this time he formed a brotherhood of seven: the Bull Demon King, Flood Dragon Demon King, Peng Demon King, Lion-Camel Demon King, Macaque King, Snub-Nosed Monkey King, and, together with them, the Handsome Monkey King himself. Every day they discussed letters and martial arts, passed the wine cups from hand to hand, sang to strings and pipes, and danced. They went at dawn and returned at dusk, and there was no pleasure they did not enjoy. A journey of ten thousand miles seemed to them no farther than the path across a courtyard. As the saying goes, a nod carried them three thousand miles, and a twist of the waist more than eight hundred.

p.src: One day, in his own cave, he ordered the four mighty commanders to prepare a banquet and invite the six kings to drink. They slaughtered oxen and horses, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, and had all the monsters dance and sing merrily until everyone was thoroughly drunk. After seeing the six kings off, he also rewarded the leaders of every rank. He reclined beneath the shade of a pine beside the Iron Slab Bridge and in a moment fell asleep. The four mighty commanders led the others in forming a protective ring around him, not daring to raise their voices. As the Handsome Monkey King slept, he saw two men approach carrying an official warrant bearing the three characters “Sun Wukong.” Without allowing him a word, they slipped a rope over him, seized the Handsome Monkey King’s soul, and dragged him stumbling and staggering straight to the edge of a city. As the Monkey King gradually emerged from his drunken stupor, he suddenly raised his head and looked. An iron plaque hung above the city, bearing three large characters: “Realm of Darkness.” The Handsome Monkey King suddenly understood and said, “The Realm of Darkness is where the King of Hell resides. Why have I come here?” The two men said, “Your allotted span in the world of light has now come to its end. We received the warrant and have summoned you here.” On hearing this, the Monkey King said, “I, Old Sun, have transcended the Three Realms and stand outside the Five Elements. I am no longer subject to his rule. How dare you blunder so blindly as to summon me?” The two collectors of the dead merely kept tugging and pulling, determined to drag him inside. This enraged the Monkey King. He drew the treasure from his ear and gave it a shake, whereupon it became as thick as a bowl. With scarcely a lift of his hand, he beat the two collectors of the dead into meat paste. He untied his own bonds, flung them aside, whirled his staff, and fought his way into the city. The ox-headed ghosts hid in every direction, while the horse-faced ghosts fled wildly north and south. The ghostly guards rushed into the Hall of the Underworld and reported, “Your Majesties, disaster! Disaster! A thunder-god with a hairy face is fighting his way in from outside!”

p.src: The Ten Kings of the Underworld were so alarmed that they hurriedly straightened their robes and came to see. Finding him fierce of countenance, they immediately took their places in order and cried aloud, “Pray give us your name, Exalted Immortal! Pray give us your name, Exalted Immortal!” The Monkey King said, “If you do not know who I am, why did you send men to seize me?” The Ten Kings replied, “We would not dare, we would not dare. Our men must have taken the wrong person.” The Monkey King said, “I am Sun Wukong, the Heaven-Born Sage of the Water-Curtain Cave on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. What offices do you hold?” Bowing, the Ten Kings said, “We are the ten sovereigns of the Underworld, the Ten Kings of the Dead.” Wukong said, “State your names quickly, and I will spare you a beating.” The Ten Kings said, “We are King Qin'guang, King Chujiang, King Songdi, King Wuguan, King Yama, King Pingdeng, King Taishan, King Dushi, King Biancheng, and the Wheel-Turning King.” Wukong said, “Since you have ascended to the rank of kings, you should be divinities possessed of spiritual perception. Why, then, can you not tell right from wrong? I, Old Sun, have cultivated immortality and attained the Way. My life is equal to Heaven's; I have risen beyond the Three Realms and leapt free of the Five Elements. Why did you have me arrested?” The Ten Kings said, “Calm your anger, Exalted Immortal. Throughout the world there are many who share the same name and surname. Could the collectors of the dead have taken the wrong road?” Wukong said, “Nonsense! Nonsense! As the saying goes, ‘Officials and clerks may err, but the man they summon does not.’ Bring me the Register of Life and Death at once, so that I may inspect it!” Hearing this, the Ten Kings invited him into the hall to examine it.

p.src: Gripping his Compliant Golden-Hooped Staff, Wukong strode straight into the Hall of the Underworld, seated himself in the center, and faced south. The Ten Kings at once ordered the judge in charge of the records to bring out the documents for inspection. The judge dared not delay. He went to the records office and brought out five or six volumes of documents together with the registers of the ten categories of living things. They examined them one by one: naked creatures, furry creatures, feathered creatures, insects, and the scaly and shelled kinds, but his name appeared nowhere. Then they came to the class of monkeys. As it turned out, this monkey resembled a human in appearance, yet was not entered among humankind; he resembled a naked creature, yet belonged to no nation; he resembled a beast, yet was not subject to the qilin; and he resembled a bird, yet was not ruled by the phoenix. There was another register, which Wukong examined himself. At last, under entry number 1,350 in the section headed “Soul,” he found the name Sun Wukong, annotated: “Heaven-born stone monkey; allotted lifespan: three hundred and forty-two years; a natural death.” Wukong said, “I do not remember how many years I was allotted, but never mind—crossing out my name will suffice. Bring me a brush.” The judge hurriedly presented a brush, loading it well with thick ink. Wukong took the registers and crossed out every name he found in the monkey category. He flung down the registers and said, “The account is settled! The account is settled! From now on, we are no longer under your rule.” Brandishing his staff all the way, he fought his way out of the Realm of Darkness. The Ten Kings dared not approach him. They all went to the Palace of Emerald Clouds, where together they paid homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and discussed submitting a memorial to Heaven. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: The Great Celestial Venerable summoned the assembled immortal civil and military ministers and asked, “In what year was this demon monkey born, and in what age did he first appear, that he has already attained such powers?” Before he had finished speaking, the Thousand-Li Eye and the Wind-Following Ear stepped out from the ranks and said, “This monkey is the heaven-born stone monkey who appeared three hundred years ago. At the time we thought nothing of it. We do not know where he has cultivated himself during these past years and become an immortal, able to subdue dragons and tame tigers and forcibly erase his name from the register of the dead.” The Jade Emperor said, “Which divine general will descend to the lower world and subdue him?” Before he had finished speaking, the Great White Star of Long Life stepped out from the ranks, prostrated himself, and memorialized: “Most Holy One, among all creatures in the Three Realms, any being with nine apertures may cultivate immortality. This monkey happens to possess a body nurtured by Heaven and Earth and a form conceived by the sun and moon. He too bears Heaven above his head and treads the earth beneath his feet, feeds on dew, and consumes the rosy clouds. Now that he has perfected the Way of Immortality and gained the power to subdue dragons and tame tigers, how does he differ from humankind? I submit that Your Majesty might extend the merciful grace that cherishes all created life and issue an imperial edict of amnesty and recruitment. Summon him to the upper realm, grant him an office great or small, enter his name in the celestial register, and keep him under restraint here. If he obeys Heaven's command, he may later be promoted and rewarded; if he defies Heaven's command, he can then be seized. Thus, first, we need not mobilize the multitude or weary the troops; and second, we shall bring an accomplished immortal into our service.” The Jade Emperor was delighted by these words and said, “We shall follow your proposal.” He immediately ordered the Star Officer of Literary Brilliance to compose the edict and the Great White Gold Star to offer amnesty and recruit the monkey.

p.src: Venus received the decree, passed out through the Southern Gate of Heaven, lowered his auspicious cloud, and went straight to the Water-Curtain Cave on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He said to the assembled young monkeys, “I am a celestial messenger sent from Heaven. I bear an imperial decree inviting your king to ascend to the celestial realm. Go and report this at once.” The young monkeys outside the cave passed the message from one to another until it reached the innermost depths of the cavern paradise: “Great King, there is an old man outside carrying a document on his back. He says he is a messenger sent from Heaven and bears an imperial decree inviting you there.” When the Handsome Monkey King heard this, he was overjoyed. “For the past two days I have been thinking of taking a trip to Heaven, and now a celestial messenger has come to invite me.” He called out, “Invite him in at once!” The Monkey King hurriedly straightened his robes and cap and went outside to welcome him. Venus went straight inside, stood in the center facing south, and said, “I am the Great White Planet Venus of the West. By the Jade Emperor’s imperial decree of amnesty and enlistment, I have descended to invite you to Heaven, where you shall be enrolled among the immortals.” Wukong smiled and said, “I am most grateful that you have deigned to visit me, venerable Star.” He ordered his underlings to prepare a banquet for their guest. Venus said, “As I bear an imperial decree, I dare not remain long. I ask Your Majesty to come with me at once. After your glorious promotion, we may converse at leisure.” Wukong said, “Thank you for honoring me with your visit. I am ashamed to send you away without hospitality, truly ashamed.” He immediately summoned his four valiant commanders and instructed them, “Take care to drill and instruct the children. I shall go up to Heaven and see what it is like; then perhaps I can take you all there to live with me.” The four valiant commanders accepted the order.
